Sixty
sĭks´ty
n. and adj. (the number 60; rendering Hebrew shishim; the AV more often says threescore)
Old English sixtig. The Authorized Version usually writes threescore; the plain word survives in the ages of Genesis 5 and the valuations of Leviticus 27.

Biblical Definition

The word stands in the ages of the fathers before the flood: “Enoch lived sixty and five years, and begat Methuselah” (Gen 5:21); “all the days of Enoch were three hundred sixty and five years” (Gen 5:23); “all the days of Methuselah were nine hundred sixty and nine years: and he died” (Gen 5:27). The Law values a vowed man “from twenty years old even unto sixty years old” at fifty shekels, and above sixty at fifteen (Lev 27:3, 7). At the dedication of the altar the princes brought “the rams sixty, the he goats sixty, the lambs of the first year sixty” (Num 7:88). And among the returning exiles, “The children of Adonikam, six hundred sixty and six” (Ezr 2:13).

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines sixty as six times ten.

SIXTY, a. Six times ten.

Key Scripture

Gen 5:23 — "And all the days of Enoch were three hundred sixty and five years:"

Gen 5:27 — "And all the days of Methuselah were nine hundred sixty and nine years: and he died."

Lev 27:3 — "And thy estimation shall be of the male from twenty years old even unto sixty years old, even thy estimation shall be fifty shekels of silver, after the shekel of the sanctuary."

Num 7:88 — "And all the oxen for the sacrifice of the peace offerings were twenty and four bullocks, the rams sixty, the he goats sixty, the lambs of the first year sixty. This was the dedication of the altar, after that it was anointed."

Ezr 2:13 — "The children of Adonikam, six hundred sixty and six."

Modern Corruption

Adonikam's six hundred sixty and six sons are pressed into the beast's number, and the Law's valuation of a man over sixty is read as contempt for age.

expand to see more

Ezra 2:13 counts six hundred sixty and six children of Adonikam coming home from Babylon, and the number means what a census means: that many people. Revelation 13:18 gives the same figure to the beast, and the number-hunters have run between the two verses ever since, as if a family of returned exiles were a cipher. Scripture uses numbers as numbers unless it says otherwise, and in Ezra it does not say otherwise. Leviticus 27 gets the opposite mistreatment: a man above sixty is valued at fifteen shekels against fifty in his prime, and the reader concludes that the Law thinks less of the old. The valuation is of labour vowed to the sanctuary, not of persons; the same chapter values a month-old child at five shekels and Scripture commands the young to rise before the hoary head (Lev 19:32). Worth and wage are different columns.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew shishim (H8346), sixty, threescore.

expand to see more

Hebrew shishim (H8346) — sixty; Genesis 5:15–27, Leviticus 27:3, 27:7, Numbers 7:88, Ezra 2:13.

Usage

"“Nine hundred sixty and nine years: and he died” — the longest life in the record, and its last clause."

"“From twenty years old even unto sixty years old” — the Law's working years."

"“The children of Adonikam, six hundred sixty and six” — a census, not a cipher."
